title: Password rejected, Caps Lock on
user_description: It keeps saying my password is incorrect, but it's the same one I always use. I've tried twice already.

options.text: Reset the password immediately without any checks
options.why: May be unnecessary and skips identity verification. Try the simplest explanations first.

options.text: Ask her to read the password out so you can try it
options.why: Never ask for or accept someone's password. Asking trains users to give passwords away, which is exactly what attackers do.

options.text: Ask her to check Caps Lock is off and to type the password slowly and carefully before changing anything
options.why: A switched-on Caps Lock key is a very common reason for rejected passwords. Checking it first costs nothing and may fix the problem without a reset.
Never the first step. It would not fix a typing mistake and destroys the user's settings.

hints: What is the simplest reason a correct password might be rejected?
Should support ever know a user's password?
real_world_tip: Tell users to use the eye icon to show what they typed. It catches most typing mistakes without anyone seeing the password.
